case_title: WAMAN & ORS. v. STATE OF MAHARASHTRA
weapon: Axes, farshas, sticks, spears, iron pipe
aggravating_circumstances: Long standing land and water dispute, use of deadly weapons, multiple assaults leading to death
trial_court_outcome: A-1 to A-6 and A-12 convicted under Sections 302, 149, 447, 147, 148; A-7, A-9, A-10, A-11 acquitted
neutral_facts: The accused and the victims were involved in a long-standing land and water dispute. On the day of the incident, the victims were working in their fields when a comment from one of the accused led to a quarrel. The accused, armed with various weapons, rushed to the scene and assaulted the victims. The victims sustained serious injuries and later succumbed to their injuries. The accused were arrested, and weapons were recovered from some of them. The trial court acquitted some accused while convicting others for offenses including murder, rioting, and causing grievous harm. The High Court upheld the trial court's decision, and the Supreme Court dismissed the appeal, finding the prosecution's case credible and the conviction justified.
